parameters.content:
## Engagement-Letter & E-Sign Pipeline

### How it works

1. Fires when a lead is marked qualified for an engagement letter (wire this to wherever your firm decides that -- an intake qualifier's hot-lead branch, or a manual staff action).
2. Resolves the client's Clio contact (reuses an existing one by email, or creates a new one), then creates a DocuSign envelope from your firm's own engagement-letter template -- filling only the fields your template already defines, never drafting language.
3. Sends the attorney a review email with an approve link. The envelope is NOT sent to the client yet -- it sits as a draft in DocuSign until the attorney approves.
4. On approval, the envelope is transitioned from draft to sent -- DocuSign delivers it to the client directly.
5. When DocuSign reports the envelope fully signed, this opens the Clio matter and notifies the firm.

**This is field population only -- it never drafts engagement terms, and nothing reaches the client until an attorney explicitly approves it.** Nothing here touches legal work (ABA Op. 512).

**This is a different deliverable from the Claude Desktop skill that drafts engagement letter text from unstructured notes** (shipped separately in the Starter Kit). This workflow assumes the letter's terms are already firm-approved in the DocuSign template -- it only fills structured fields, sends for signature, and opens the matter.

### Setup steps

- [ ] Build your firm's engagement letter as a DocuSign template with text tabs for the fields this fills (see deploy guide for the exact tab labels).
- [ ] Configure a DocuSign OAuth2 credential and a Clio OAuth2 credential (reuse if already deployed).
- [ ] Create a Google Sheet with an 'Engagement Pipeline' tab -- see the deploy guide for exact columns.
- [ ] Configure Google Sheets OAuth2 and SMTP credentials.
- [ ] Set the required n8n Variables: FIRM_NAME, FIRM_FROM_EMAIL, FIRM_ATTORNEY_EMAIL, CLIO_BASE_URL, DOCUSIGN_AUTH_BASE_URL, ENGAGEMENT_LETTER_TEMPLATE_ID, ENGAGEMENT_LETTER_ROLE_NAME, ENGAGEMENT_PIPELINE_SHEET_ID, ENGAGEMENT_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL.
- [ ] Register a DocuSign Connect webhook pointed at this workflow's signature-completed URL (see deploy guide).
- [ ] Activate the workflow.

### Customization

The text tab list in 'Build Engagement Letter Envelope Request' must match your DocuSign template's own field labels exactly -- edit that list, not the surrounding logic, to match your actual template.

## Qualified lead intake, contact resolution, and draft envelope

Resolves the Clio contact and creates a DocuSign envelope as a draft -- filling firm-approved fields only, never sent to the client yet.

## Attorney review request

Logs the pending envelope and emails the attorney a review link -- nothing reaches the client until this is approved.

## Attorney approval — a second, independent branch

On approval, transitions the DocuSign envelope from draft to sent -- DocuSign delivers it to the client directly, this workflow never emails the client itself.

## Signature completed — a third, independent branch

DocuSign Connect notifies this workflow when the envelope is fully signed. Opens the Clio matter and notifies the firm.

nodes.name: When Lead Qualified For Engagement
nodes.notes: Wire this to wherever your firm decides a lead is ready for an engagement letter -- an intake qualifier's hot-lead branch, or a manual staff action -- POSTing the lead's name, email, phone, practice area, case details, and assigned attorney.

nodes.name: Parse Qualified Lead Data
nodes.notes: Field names match a generic 'lead qualified' payload -- adjust to match whatever actually triggers this (your intake qualifier, CRM, or a manual form).

nodes.name: Fetch Existing Clio Contact
nodes.notes: Searches Clio by email so a returning lead reuses their existing contact instead of creating a duplicate.

nodes.name: Determine If Contact Exists
nodes.notes: Matches on exact email -- Clio's own query search can return near-matches, so this narrows to a real match before deciding whether to create a new contact.

nodes.name: If Contact Exists In Clio
nodes.notes: Reuses an existing contact when found; creates a new one otherwise.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ data: { type: 'Person', name: $json.full_name, primary_email_address: $json.email, primary_phone_number: $json.phone } }) }}

nodes.name: Create New Clio Contact
nodes.notes: Only runs when no existing contact matched by email.

parameters.jsCode:
const lead = $('Determine If Contact Exists').item.json;
return { json: { ...lead, contact_id: $json.data.id } };

nodes.name: Merge New Contact Id
nodes.notes: Reads lead data back from 'Determine If Contact Exists' by name, not $json, since the Clio create call in between replaces $json with its own response.

parameters.jsCode:
const lead = $json;
return { json: { ...lead, contact_id: lead.existing_contact_id } };

nodes.name: Use Existing Contact Id
nodes.notes: Only runs when an existing contact matched by email.

nodes.name: Fetch DocuSign User Info
nodes.notes: Resolves the DocuSign account's base_uri and account_id -- both required to call the envelopes API. Same pattern already used in Form-Fill from Intake Data (OPS5).

nodes.name: Build Engagement Letter Envelope Request
nodes.notes: ENGAGEMENT_LETTER_TEMPLATE_ID and ENGAGEMENT_LETTER_ROLE_NAME point at your firm's own pre-approved DocuSign template -- this never generates new legal language, only fills its existing fields.

nodes.name: Post Draft Envelope To DocuSign
nodes.notes: Creates the envelope as a draft only -- status stays 'created', nothing is sent to the client at this point.

nodes.name: Parse Envelope Creation Response
nodes.notes: Reads the previous node's raw response, not $json passthrough -- surfaces a creation failure to the attorney instead of silently stopping.

parameters.jsCode:
const d = $json;
return { json: { ...d, review_id: 'ENGL-' + Date.now() } };

nodes.name: Assign Review Id
nodes.notes: Ties the tracking sheet row to this engagement letter and is the key the attorney's approval link comes back with.

nodes.name: Log Engagement For Review
nodes.notes: Every qualified lead gets a row here, even one whose envelope creation failed -- a visible record for the attorney to follow up on manually. Column headers must match exactly.

nodes.name: Build Attorney Review Request Email
nodes.notes: ENGAGEMENT_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL is this workflow's own Production URL for the approval webhook below -- set it after activating.

nodes.name: Send Attorney Review Request Email
nodes.notes: Internal notification to firm staff, not the client -- no compliance guardrail wrap needed.

nodes.name: Attorney Decision Request Trigger
nodes.notes: Receives the attorney's click on the approve link from the review email. This URL is what ENGAGEMENT_DECISION_WEBHOOK_URL should point to.

nodes.name: Parse Attorney Decision Request
nodes.notes: Only 'approve' is a supported action -- there is no reject/decline link because declining just means the attorney never clicks approve.

nodes.name: If Attorney Decision Valid
nodes.notes: Catches a malformed or tampered link before it touches the tracking sheet.

nodes.name: Respond Invalid Attorney Decision
nodes.notes: Shown when the approval link is malformed or already used.

nodes.name: Read Engagement Pipeline Log
nodes.notes: Reads the whole tracking sheet so the review_id can be matched by exact value -- more reliable in this environment than a computed row-number match.

nodes.name: Find Matching Engagement Row
nodes.notes: Matches the approval link's review_id against the tracking sheet by exact value -- more reliable than a computed row-number match in this environment.

nodes.name: If Engagement Row Found
nodes.notes: Confirms the review_id from the link actually matches a logged engagement before touching DocuSign.

parameters.responseBody: We couldn't find that engagement letter -- it may have already been approved or the link is malformed.

nodes.name: Respond Engagement Not Found
nodes.notes: Shown when the review_id in the link doesn't match any row -- the engagement may have already been approved.

nodes.name: Fetch DocuSign Account Info For Send
nodes.notes: This is a separate webhook execution from the draft-creation branch, so the account info is re-fetched here rather than reused.

nodes.name: Transition Envelope To Sent
nodes.notes: This is the moment the client actually receives the engagement letter -- DocuSign emails it to them directly once this call succeeds. This workflow never emails the client itself.

nodes.name: Parse Envelope Send Response
nodes.notes: Reads DocuSign's response to the send call so a failure is recorded and shown to the attorney instead of silently succeeding.

nodes.name: Update Engagement Row As Sent
nodes.notes: Marks the row sent (or send_failed) so the pipeline sheet always reflects the true DocuSign state.

parameters.responseBody:
={{ '

' + ($json.sent_ok ? '✅ Sent for signature' : '⚠️ Could not send') + '

' + $json.full_name + ($json.sent_ok ? ' has been sent the engagement letter for signature.' : ' -- DocuSign error: ' + $json.send_error) + '

' }}

nodes.name: Respond Attorney Decision Confirmation
nodes.notes: Confirms to the attorney whether the letter was actually sent to the client.

nodes.name: DocuSign Signature Webhook
nodes.notes: Register this URL as a DocuSign Connect webhook (Admin > Connect) subscribed to the Envelope Completed event, so this fires automatically the moment the client finishes signing.

nodes.name: Parse DocuSign Signature Event
nodes.notes: Guard pattern for external webhooks -- DocuSign Connect fires on every envelope status change, not just completion, so non-completion events must be routed away rather than processed.

nodes.name: If Envelope Fully Signed
nodes.notes: Guard pattern for external webhooks -- routes anything other than a genuine completion event to the skip branch instead of processing it.

nodes.name: Skip — Not A Completion Event
nodes.notes: Non-actionable DocuSign Connect events (viewed, delivered, declined, etc.) land here and are ignored.

nodes.name: Respond Skipped Event
nodes.notes: Acknowledges the webhook call to DocuSign so it doesn't retry a non-actionable event.

nodes.name: Read Pipeline Log For Signature
nodes.notes: Reads the tracking sheet so the signed envelope can be matched back to its lead and Clio contact.

nodes.name: Find Matching Signed Row
nodes.notes: Matches the signed envelope_id against the tracking sheet by exact value.

nodes.name: If Signed Row Found
nodes.notes: Confirms the signed envelope actually matches a row before opening a Clio matter.

nodes.name: Respond Signed Row Not Found
nodes.notes: Still returns 200 to DocuSign (so it doesn't retry indefinitely) even though no matching row was found -- check the sheet manually if this happens.

parameters.jsonBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ data: { client: { id: Number($json.contact_id) }, practice_area: { name: $json.practice_area }, description: `Engagement letter signed -- ${$json.full_name}`, status: 'Open' } }) }}

nodes.name: Create New Clio Matter
nodes.notes: Opens the matter under the same Clio contact resolved when the envelope was created -- reuses PAC-20's create-matter pattern.

nodes.name: Parse Matter Creation Response
nodes.notes: Reads Clio's response to confirm the matter was actually created before marking the row complete.

nodes.name: Update Engagement Row As Signed
nodes.notes: Marks the row signed and records the new matter ID, so staff can see at a glance which clients are now active matters.

parameters.subject: ={{ 'Engagement letter signed: ' + $json.full_name }}
parameters.text: ={{ $json.full_name + ' has signed their engagement letter. ' + ($json.matter_created ? ('A new matter has been opened in Clio (matter ID ' + $json.matter_id + ').') : 'The Clio matter could not be created automatically -- please open it manually.') }}

nodes.name: Notify Staff Of Signed Engagement
nodes.notes: Internal staff notification -- lets the team know the client relationship is now active and where to find the matter.

nodes.name: Respond Signature Processed
nodes.notes: Acknowledges the webhook call to DocuSign.
